issues.subject: [ie/youtube] Fix PO token sanitization for Python 3.15 (#16884)
issues.title: Test failures with yt-dlp 2026.03.17 and Python 3.15.0b2
issues.desc:
We are working on rebuilding all Python packages in Fedora Linux for Python 3.15.0b2. This part of our effort to catch issues and work with upstream projects to resolve them before new Python versions become GA.

There are currently a couple test failures related to PO tokens when running pytest with Python 3.15.0b2 and yt-dlp 2026.03.17. They are reproduced below. See https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org//work/tasks/2982/146232982/build.log for full logs (search for "/usr/bin/pytest" to find the pytest run).

issues.subject: [ie/reddit] Fix unauthenticated extraction (#16839)

issues.desc:
For a couple days now, when attempting to download any reddit video, I get the "Account authentication is required" error message. This is thrown whenever the JSON metadata cannot be parsed (presumably because it's actually HTML in this case), therefor, this echoes the issue spam of #9714, #9912, #10107, and #10924 from people who's IP addresses got flagged as suspicious and therefor needed to log in to view the content. Thing is, I haven't really been hammering reddit much at all, nor am I connecting from a datacenter IP; but more importantly, opening the link in a browser plays the video just fine. What's going on?

#### Clues:
- If I navigate to the video in the browser and subsequently try to download the video with `--cookies-from-browser`, it works. With a clean cookie jar, it doesn'

issues.subject: [ie/niconico] Fix error detection (#16991)
issues.title: [niconico] KeyError('data') on device-restricted videos
issues.desc:
The niconico extractor fails with KeyError('data') when attempting to download
device-restricted videos (videos that require login due to device limitations).

Non-restricted videos may work fine. The issue is specific to videos that are
flagged as sensitive/device-restricted content requiring authentication.

I verified that the video is accessible in a browser while logged in with cookies,
and the correct API response (via ?responseType=json) does contain a "data" key
with full video/media information including domand video streams.
However, yt-dlp's extractor fails to parse the response correctly.

The working API response contains:
- data.response.media.domand with video/audio stream info
- data.response.video with video metadata

issues.subject: [ie/youtube:tab] Fix flat extraction of collaborators (#17045)
issues.title: The uploader metadata for videos in playlists with multiple uploaders on a YouTube channel is missing
issues.desc:
The issue I describe here is the same as the one I reported here - https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16952 - however, I've found that the fix only works for videos with a single uploader and the issue remains for videos with multiple uploaders (a fairly new YouTube feature). I mentioned this in a reply to the previous bug report, but I did not receive a response, so I deleted it and created this thread. In the Verbose Output, I've provided an example playlist that demonstrates this issue.

ydl_opts = {
    'quiet': True,
    'verbose': True,
    'extract_flat': 'True',
    'skip_download': True,
    'ignoreerrors': True,
}

issues.subject: [ie/instagram] Fix logged-in extraction (#17278)
issues.title: [Instagram] Video info extraction failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found (with cookies)
issues.desc:
It looks like Instagram is rolling out their GraphQL API.
Yesterday this command worked for me: `yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome -j "https://www.instagram.com/p/Da0nIK8pENz/"` but today it returns:

> ERROR: [Instagram] Da0nIK8pENz: Video info extraction failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found (caused by <HTTPError 404: Not Found>)

It looks like `yt-dlp` uses `media/<id>/info` Instagram API which might have been decommissioned, as now I see only `POST /api/graphql` GraphQL API requests in my network tab.

I forgot to mention that I am logged in my Chrome.
